title: Cooking with Chris: Recreating a Culinary Icon from Waldorf Astoria New York
summary: Hilton President & CEO Chris Nassetta recreates one of the most famous dishes to emerge from Waldorf Astoria New York: the Waldorf Salad.

Hilton President & CEO Chris Nassetta joins acclaimed Chef Michael Anthony to revisit the legendary Waldorf Salad and celebrate more than a century of food and beverage history


- **In “Cooking with Chris,” Hilton President & CEO Chris Nassetta continues his culinary journey alongside Chef Michael Anthony of Waldorf Astoria New York, recreating one of the most famous dishes to emerge from this legendary hotel: the Waldorf Salad.**
- **Discover the story behind a dish that began with a simple combination of apples, celery and mayonnaise and became an enduring American classic, inspiring countless interpretations around the world.**
- **Go inside the kitchen with Chris and Chef Michael as they explore how Waldorf Astoria’s culinary legacy continues to inspire a new generation while giving this storied dish a fresh, contemporary spin that evolves with the seasons.**


For more than a century, the Waldorf Salad has carried the name of one of the world’s most legendary hotels to dining tables around the globe. Crisp apples, celery and a creamy dressing formed the foundation of a surprisingly simple creation that would become both an American classic and an enduring part of the culinary legacy of[Waldorf Astoria New York](https://www.waldorfastorianewyork.com/) .


In the latest episode of “Cooking with Chris,” Hilton President & CEO Chris Nassetta welcomes[Chef Michael Anthony](https://www.hilton.com/en/travel/articles/chef-michael-anthony-at-waldorf-astoria-new-york/) to the new test kitchen at Hilton Global Headquarters in Virginia, a space designed for chefs and Hilton teams to test, learn and explore new food and beverage ideas. Here, they revisit this iconic dish and explore the history, creativity and hospitality behind it.


## A Recipe with a Storied Past


-
-


*The Cookbook by "Oscar" at The Waldorf*


The story of the Waldorf Salad stretches back to the late 19th century and the original Waldorf Hotel in New York City. The dish is widely credited to Oscar Tschirky, the hotel’s legendary maître d’hôtel, who included a recipe for “Waldorf Salad” in his 1896 cookbook, *The Cook Book by “Oscar” of the Waldorf* .


The original was straightforward, mixing apples and celery dressed with mayonnaise and served on lettuce. Walnuts, now one of the ingredients most closely associated with the salad, were added in later interpretations. But from these humble beginnings, the Waldorf Salad took on a life of its own. Over the decades, chefs and home cooks experimented with the recipe, adding everything from grapes and nuts to new dressings and seasonal ingredients.


In this video, Chef Michael brings that history into the kitchen, sharing an original 1896 copy of the cookbook, while also sharing some of the exciting ways that he’s bringing this history-rich dish into the modern era by adding his own seasonal spin on the recipe, which he dubs the “New Waldorf Salad.”


This spirit of honoring the past while staying relevant in a modern world is particularly fitting for Waldorf Astoria New York, which has entered a new chapter following its[highly anticipated return in 2025](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/waldorf-astoria-new-york-begins-opening-season) . Now, fresh energy has been brought to one of New York City’s most storied addresses while preserving the history that made it an icon. And Chef Michael is helping shape the hotel’s next culinary era.


## Bringing an Iconic Dish to Life


-
-
-


Chef Michael Anthony and Chris Nassetta


Chef Michael brings more than three decades of culinary experience to Waldorf Astoria New York, with a career that’s earned him numerous accolades, including James Beard Awards for Outstanding Chef and Best Chef: New York City.


His approach to cooking is grounded in a simple philosophy: thoughtful dishes don’t need to be overcomplicated. Instead, he looks to seasonal ingredients, responsible sourcing and carefully considered flavors to create food that feels both memorable and approachable. At the hotel’s signature, American Brasserie-style restaurant[Lex Yard](https://www.lexyardnyc.com/) , the focus is on seasonal American cooking that draws inspiration from the past while reflecting the way New Yorkers and travelers want to eat today. The restaurant reflects Chef Michael’s deep relationships with local farmers and producers, with each plate composed to reflect New York’s agricultural calendar. With its balance of design, storytelling and seasonality, Lex Yard is a love letter to the city it calls home.


“When you taste a dish at Lex Yard, you really want to know what time of year it is,” said Chef Michael Anthony. “And that's the idea; anchoring that memory in a particular time and place.”


This philosophy comes through in his execution of the New Waldorf Salad. His goal, he explains, is to remain faithful to the original while making the dish “craveable” and ensuring it doesn’t become stagnant. For fall, that means adding ingredients such as roasted celery root and delicate squash. In spring, he might turn to pea shoots, snow peas, sugar snap peas and asparagus, while summer can bring stone fruit, tomatoes and basil.


Watch as Chris works alongside Chef Michael to bring two versions of the Waldorf Salad to life, mixing up ingredients, swapping stories, and sharing a few tricks of the trade as they uncover how a handful of simple ingredients became a dish synonymous with one of the world’s most iconic hotels.


Want to bring a taste of Waldorf Astoria history into your own kitchen? Find the full Waldorf Salad recipe below and recreate this legendary dish at home.


## New Waldorf Salad


A modern reinterpretation of the Waldorf Astoria's signature salad, first created at the hotel in the 1890s. The dish is rebuilt with dressed Little Gem lettuce, celery, Honeycrisp apple, red grapes, candied walnuts, and cheddar, finished with a bright lemon dressing and house-made aioli. The recipe below is presented in production quantities as prepared by the culinary team and may be scaled for tasting purposes. The salad recipe represents roughly 4 servings. The aioli, dressing and candied walnuts can be made ahead and used to personal taste.


### Ingredients


#### Aioli


- Grapeseed oil 900 g
- Egg yolks 6 ea
- Dijon mustard 55 g
- Lemon juice 2 ea
- Garlic, microplaned 3 ea
- Salt 10 g


#### Lemon Dressing


- Lemons, juiced and peeled 5 ea
- Lemon oil 100 g
- Extra virgin olive oil 50 g
- Honey 168 g
- Champagne vinegar 65 g


#### Candied Walnuts


- Walnuts 400 g
- Sugar 400 g
- Grapeseed oil as needed


#### Assembly to Serve


- Little Gem lettuce, chiffonade 100 g
- Market herbs 30 g
- Celery, sliced on bias (“U” cuts) 100 g
- Honeycrisp apples, julienned 50 g
- Red grapes, halved 75 g
- Candied walnuts 30 g
- Sunflower seeds, toasted 15 g
- Cheddar cheese (half small-diced, half grated) 100 g
- Aioli 30 g
- Lemon dressing 100 g


### Directions


#### Aioli Instructions


- In a blender, combine egg yolks, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice; blend until frothy.
- Stream in grapeseed oil gradually until fully emulsified.
- Reserve in a covered container until needed.


#### Lemon Dressing Instructions


- Blanch the lemon peels three times.
- Combine all ingredients except the oils in a blender.
- Gradually add the oils, finishing with the olive oil, until emulsified.
- Adjust seasoning with honey, salt, and pepper as needed.


#### Candied Walnuts Instructions


- Combine sugar with an equal amount of water and the lemon juice; bring to a boil.
- Add walnuts and cook until tender, but not fully candied.
- Drain through a fine mesh strainer and spread on a parchment-lined sheet tray.
- Toast at 325°F, low fan, 12–15 minutes, until shiny and crisp.
- Cool completely before handling — sugar retains high heat. Reserve in a clean, dry container.


#### Assembly to Serve


- In a mixing bowl, toss the Little Gem lettuce with a small amount of lemon dressing; season with salt and pepper.
- Spoon a small pool of lemon dressing in the center of a salad bowl and top with the dressed Little Gem, spread slightly.
- In the same mixing bowl, toss the celery “U”s, apple julienne, grape halves, aioli, and candied walnuts; season with salt and pepper.
- Spoon this mixture over the dressed Little Gem.
- Finish with toasted sunflower seeds and a grating of cheddar cheese over the top.


### Cook’s Note


SEASONAL VARIATIONS
- Summer: Add oven-roasted stone fruit; substitute ricotta salata for cheddar.
- Autumn: Add toasted pumpkin seeds and roasted delicata squash.
- Winter: Add celery root rémoulade.
- Spring: Add blanched English and snow peas; garnish with mint and pea tendrils.


## The Original 1896 Recipe


Cooking with Chris - The Waldorf Salad - The Original 1896 Recipe


The Waldorf Salad was created by Hotel Maître d’ Oscar Tschirky, whose innovations shaped many of the Waldorf Astoria’s most celebrated dishes. The original recipes below are reproduced as they appear in his 1896 volume, The Cook Book by “Oscar” of the Waldorf.


**Waldorf Salad**


Peel two raw apples and cut them into small pieces, say about a half an inch square, also cut some celery the same way, and mix it with the apple. Be very careful not to let any seeds of the apples be mixed with it. The salad must be dressed with a good mayonnaise.


**Good Mayonnaise**


Place in an earthen bowl a couple of fresh egg yolks, and half a teaspoonful of ground English mustard, half a pinch of salt, half a teaspoonful of red pepper, and stir well for about 3 minutes without stopping, then pour in, drop at a time, one and a half cupfuls of the best olive oil, and should it become too thick, add a little at a time, some good vinegar, stirring constantly.


Source: *The Cook Book by “Oscar” of the Waldorf* , Oscar Tschirky, c. 1896.
